1	"""Core service surface for StreamMill.
2	
3	The frozen baseline only reports process health; that surface stays
4	unchanged. On top of it this module now implements named event-time
5	tumbling windows with explicit watermarks:
6	
7	* streams are created with a positive ``window_ms`` and a non-negative
8	  ``allowed_lateness_ms``;
9	* events carry an integer ``timestamp_ms`` and a finite numeric ``value``
10	  and land in the left-closed, right-open window
11	  ``[floor(timestamp_ms / window_ms) * window_ms, +window_ms)``;
12	* a per-stream watermark only moves forward; once it reaches
13	  ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` the window is final, is
14	  emitted exactly once, and is retained for queries;
15	* events with ``timestamp_ms < watermark - allowed_lateness_ms`` are
16	  acknowledged but dropped without touching the aggregates.
17	
18	Streams may optionally be created with a positive ``slide_ms`` (no
19	larger than ``window_ms`` and dividing it evenly). Such streams use
20	fixed-step overlapping sliding windows: an accepted event at timestamp
21	``t`` is counted once in every window ``[start, start + window_ms)``
22	whose ``start`` is an integer multiple of ``slide_ms`` and satisfies
23	``start <= t < start + window_ms`` (negative timestamps follow the same
24	mathematical grid). Every window still finalizes independently once the
25	watermark reaches its own ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` and is
26	emitted exactly once, ordered by window start. Without ``slide_ms`` the
27	stream is the plain tumbling stream above and every public shape is
28	unchanged.
29	
30	Streams may optionally enable event-id deduplication by passing a
31	positive ``dedup_retention_ms`` (no smaller than ``allowed_lateness_ms``)
32	at creation time. On such streams every event must carry a non-empty
33	string ``event_id``:
34	
35	* the first occurrence of an id is aggregated and remembered together
36	  with its ``timestamp_ms`` and ``value``;
37	* an exact retry (same ``timestamp_ms`` and numerically equal ``value``)
38	  is reported as ``duplicate: true`` and never touches the aggregates —
39	  the dedup check runs before the lateness check, so retained retries
40	  are duplicates even past the lateness horizon;
41	* the same id with a different timestamp or value is rejected with
42	  ``event_id_conflict`` and leaves all state untouched;
43	* an unseen id that arrives too late is dropped as usual and its id is
44	  not remembered.
45	
46	Remembered ids are evicted once the watermark advances past
47	``timestamp_ms + dedup_retention_ms`` (ids exactly on the boundary are
48	kept); evicted ids may be reused and are treated as new events.
49	
50	Streams created with a non-negative ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` track the
51	maximum ``timestamp_ms`` of every successfully accepted event. After an
52	event is aggregated (and its id registered, when deduplicating) the
53	watermark advances atomically to
54	``max(current_watermark, max_event_timestamp - auto_watermark_lag_ms)``;
55	the lateness/dedup decision for that event uses the watermark as it was
56	before the advance. Dropped, duplicate or conflicting events never move
57	the maximum event timestamp or the watermark. Manual watermark posts keep
58	working on automatic streams and subsequent automatic advances never
59	regress below a manual watermark. Event responses on automatic streams
60	additionally carry the post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``null`` until a
61	watermark exists) and the windows finalized by that response.
62	
63	A portable full-state snapshot is available through
64	``Service.snapshot`` / ``Service.restore_snapshot``: export produces a
65	self-contained JSON document (``format_version`` 1) capturing config,
66	watermark, open windows, finalized results and retained dedup records;
67	automatic streams additionally carry ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` and
68	``max_event_timestamp_ms``; sliding streams additionally carry
69	``slide_ms`` (a document without it restores as a tumbling stream).
70	Restore is only accepted on an instance
71	without any streams, validates the document strictly (never silently
72	repairing it) and publishes the whole state atomically.
73	
74	In-process dimension tables provide the lookup side of an optional
75	current-value stream-table join:
76	
77	* ``POST /tables`` creates a named table; rows are written with
78	  ``PUT``-style upserts of non-empty string ``key``/``label`` pairs and
79	  report whether the stored label actually ``changed``;
80	* a stream may be created with ``lookup_table`` naming an existing
81	  table. Events on such a stream must carry a non-empty ``lookup_key``;
82	  after the usual dedup and lateness decisions the current label is read
83	  atomically (an unknown key is rejected with ``lookup_key_not_found``
84	  and leaves all state untouched) and the event is aggregated both into
85	  the plain windows and into per-window ``(lookup_key, label)`` groups.
86	  Later table writes only affect later events. Dedup records on joined
87	  streams include the ``lookup_key``, so resubmitting an id with a
88	  different key is an ``event_id_conflict``;
89	* joined groups finalize together with their window and are exposed
90	  through ``Service.joined_results``, ordered by window start, lookup
91	  key and label.
92	
93	Snapshots export as ``format_version`` 2 (adding ``tables`` plus
94	``lookup_table``/``joined_windows``/``joined_finalized`` on joined
95	streams) whenever any table exists, and restore stays compatible with
96	version 1 documents. When the join is unused every public shape and the
97	version 1 snapshot are unchanged.
98	
99	Streams may optionally materialize a window change feed by passing a
100	positive ``change_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the create
101	response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before). On such
102	streams every state change is published as a totally ordered sequence of
103	records, numbered by a ``seq`` that starts at 1 and never regresses:
104	
105	* every successfully aggregated event appends one ``upsert`` record per
106	  affected base window (ascending by window start on sliding streams),
107	  carrying the post-event ``count``/``sum`` of that window;
108	* every watermark advance that finalizes windows appends one ``final``
109	  record per newly finalized window (ascending by window start) with the
110	  final aggregates — on automatic streams the upserts of the triggering
111	  event always precede the finals of the resulting advance, and an
112	  advance without newly finalized windows appends nothing;
113	* duplicates, too-late drops, conflicts, unknown lookup keys and
114	  validation failures never consume a sequence number, and joined
115	  streams publish only the base-window changes.
116	
117	``Service.changes`` returns the retained records with ``seq`` greater
118	than a cursor, ascending, together with the current ``latest_seq``.
119	Only the newest ``change_retention`` records are kept (older ones are
120	trimmed after every commit, without moving ``latest_seq``); a cursor
121	past ``latest_seq`` raises ChangeCursorAheadError and a cursor that has
122	fallen behind the oldest retained record raises
123	ChangeCursorExpiredError.
124	
125	Instances with at least one change-feed stream export snapshots as
126	``format_version`` 3, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
127	enabled streams, ``change_retention``/``latest_seq``/``changes``.
128	Restore validates the retained records strictly (sequence continuity
129	against ``latest_seq`` and the retention cap, ordering, window
130	alignment, and the last retained record of every window against the
131	aggregated state) and publishes the feed so the cursor and the next
132	sequence number continue exactly as on the uninterrupted instance.
133	Version 1 and 2 documents restore as before, and instances without a
134	change feed keep exporting their original versions and shapes.
135	
136	Streams may optionally enable recoverable atomic batch ingestion by
137	passing a positive ``batch_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the
138	create response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before and the
139	batch entry point raises BatchIngestNotEnabledError). On such streams
140	``Service.add_batch`` accepts a non-empty ``batch_id`` plus 1 to 1000
141	events that each follow the stream's single-event rules:
142	
143	* the whole batch is applied at one consistent point, in input order and
144	  under the service lock, reusing the per-event dedup, lateness, lookup,
145	  window, automatic-watermark, finalization and change-feed semantics —
146	  no concurrent request can observe an intermediate state, and on
147	  automatic streams each element sees the watermark left by the
148	  previous one;
149	* the first event-id conflict or unknown lookup key aborts the batch and
150	  rolls back every state the earlier elements touched (aggregates, dedup
151	  records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and change
152	  sequence), so a failed batch leaves the stream exactly as before and
153	  does not occupy its identifier; too-late drops and exact duplicates
154	  remain successful outcomes;
155	* a successful batch is remembered together with its request and full
156	  response. Within the retention a retry carrying the same field values
157	  in the same event order replays the stored response without writing
158	  again (and without refreshing the retention order), while the same
159	  ``batch_id`` with different content raises BatchIdConflictError. Only
160	  the newest ``batch_retention`` records are kept; evicted identifiers
161	  may be reused, and concurrent submissions of one identifier commit at
162	  most once.
163	
164	Instances with at least one batch-enabled stream export snapshots as
165	``format_version`` 4, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
166	enabled streams, ``batch_retention`` plus the retained batch records in
167	commit order. Restore validates the records strictly (identifier
168	uniqueness, the retention cap, and the request/response shapes against
169	the stream's features) and publishes them so replay and eviction behave
170	exactly as on the uninterrupted instance. Older document versions
171	restore as before.
172	
173	Dimension tables may optionally be declared event-time versioned by
174	passing ``event_time_versioned: true`` at creation time (echoed in the
175	create response; without it the table keeps the current-value overwrite
176	semantics above and every public shape is unchanged). A versioned table
177	receives rows of ``key``/``label``/``effective_from_ms`` through the
178	same row entry point: each version of a key is effective from its
179	``effective_from_ms`` until the key's next version, writes may arrive
180	out of order, a first write or a new effective time reports
181	``changed: true``, an identical retry reports ``changed: false``, and
182	an existing ``(key, effective_from_ms)`` point resubmitted with a
183	different label raises DimensionVersionConflictError and leaves the
184	history untouched. A stream whose ``lookup_table`` is versioned
185	resolves every event's label as the newest version with
186	``effective_from_ms <= timestamp_ms`` — late-arriving or backfilled
187	history therefore only affects events whose own event time it precedes
188	and never recomputes already received events; an unknown key or an
189	event time before the key's first version raises
190	LookupVersionNotFoundError with all state untouched. Dedup, lateness,
191	windowing, watermarks, change-feed sequence numbers and batch
192	atomicity (a missing version anywhere rolls the whole batch back) are
193	exactly as on current-value joins.
194	
195	Instances with at least one versioned table export snapshots as
196	``format_version`` 5, which always carries the ``tables`` array; each
197	table object records its mode, and versioned tables export their rows
198	as ``versions`` strictly ordered by ``key`` then ``effective_from_ms``.
199	Restore stays compatible with versions 1 to 4 and validates version 5
200	strictly (mode field combinations, duplicate or out-of-order versions,
201	invalid effective times and conflicting points all raise SnapshotError
202	without publishing partial state).
203	
204	Disk persistence remains out of scope.
205	"""

303	class _Table:
304	    """Mutable state of one dimension table. Guarded by the Service lock.
305	
306	    A current-value table keeps one label per key in ``rows``. An
307	    event-time versioned table instead keeps, per key, a timeline of
308	    ``(effective_from_ms, label)`` points strictly ascending by
309	    ``effective_from_ms``; a point is effective until the key's next
310	    point, and points may be inserted out of order.
311	    """
312	
313	    def __init__(self, event_time_versioned: bool = False) -> None:
314	        self.event_time_versioned = event_time_versioned
315	        # Current-value mode: key -> label.
316	        self.rows: dict[str, str] = {}
317	        # Versioned mode: key -> [(effective_from_ms, label), ...]
318	        self.versions: dict[str, list[tuple[int, str]]] = {}
319	
320	    def put_version(self, key: str, label: str, effective_from_ms: int) -> bool:
321	        """Insert one version point; return True when the history changed.
322	
323	        An identical retry of an existing point leaves the history
324	        untouched and reports no change; the same point with a different
325	        label is a conflict and also leaves the history untouched.
326	        """
327	        timeline = self.versions.setdefault(key, [])
328	        index = bisect.bisect_left(
329	            timeline, effective_from_ms, key=lambda point: point[0]
330	        )
331	        if index < len(timeline) and timeline[index][0] == effective_from_ms:
332	            if timeline[index][1] == label:
333	                return False
334	            raise DimensionVersionConflictError(
335	                f"version ({key!r}, {effective_from_ms}) already exists with a "
336	                f"different label"
337	            )
338	        timeline.insert(index, (effective_from_ms, label))
339	        return True
340	
341	    def label_at(self, key: str, timestamp_ms: int) -> str:
342	        """Newest label of ``key`` effective at ``timestamp_ms``.
343	
344	        Raises LookupVersionNotFoundError when the key is unknown or the
345	        timestamp precedes its first version.
346	        """
347	        timeline = self.versions.get(key)
348	        if not timeline:
349	            raise LookupVersionNotFoundError(key)
350	        index = (
351	            bisect.bisect_right(timeline, timestamp_ms, key=lambda point: point[0])
352	            - 1
353	        )
354	        if index < 0:
355	            raise LookupVersionNotFoundError(key)
356	        return timeline[index][1]

361	
362	    def __init__(
363	        self,
364	        name: str,
365	        window_ms: int,
366	        allowed_lateness_ms: int,
367	        dedup_retention_ms: int | None = None,
368	        auto_watermark_lag_ms: int | None = None,

370	        lookup_table: str | None = None,
371	        change_retention: int | None = None,
372	        batch_retention: int | None = None,

374	        self.name = name
375	        self.window_ms = window_ms
376	        self.allowed_lateness_ms = allowed_lateness_ms
377	        self.dedup_retention_ms = dedup_retention_ms
378	        self.auto_watermark_lag_ms = auto_watermark_lag_ms
379	        # None selects the tumbling grid (step == window_ms); otherwise the
380	        # stream is sliding with this fixed, evenly-dividing step.
381	        self.slide_ms = slide_ms
382	        # Name of the dimension table this stream joins against, if any.
383	        self.lookup_table = lookup_table

392	        # maintained on automatic streams, None until the first such event.
393	        self.max_event_timestamp: int | None = None
394	        # window_start_ms -> [count, sum]; only non-empty windows exist.
395	        self._windows: dict[int, list] = {}
396	        self._finalized: list[dict] = []
397	        self._finalized_starts: set[int] = set()
398	        # event_id -> (timestamp_ms, value) for accepted, not yet evicted
399	        # ids; joined streams append the lookup_key to the tuple.
400	        self._dedup: dict[str, tuple] = {}
401	        # Joined streams only: window_start_ms -> (lookup_key, label) ->
402	        # [count, sum] for open windows, plus the finalized group rows in
403	        # results order (window start, lookup_key, label).
404	        self._joined_windows: dict[int, dict[tuple[str, str], list]] = {}
405	        self._joined_finalized: list[dict] = []
406	        # Change feed: the next record gets _latest_seq + 1; _changes
407	        # holds at most change_retention records, oldest first.
408	        self._latest_seq = 0
409	        self._changes: list[dict] = []
410	        # Retained batch records in commit order, at most batch_retention
411	        # of them; each is {"batch_id", "request", "response"}.

415	    def _step_ms(self) -> int:
416	        """Grid spacing: slide_ms for sliding streams, else window_ms."""
417	        return self.slide_ms if self.slide_ms is not None else self.window_ms
418	
419	    def _window_starts(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[int]:
420	        """Starts of every grid window covering ``timestamp_ms``.
421	
422	        Windows are ``[start, start + window_ms)`` with ``start`` on the
423	        grid of multiples of the step; the floor division keeps the same
424	        boundaries for negative timestamps. The list is ascending, which
425	        is also the finalization/results order.
426	        """
427	        step = self._step_ms
428	        last = (timestamp_ms // step) * step
429	        first = last - (self.window_ms - step)
430	        return list(range(first, last + 1, step))

432	    def add_event(
433	        self,
434	        timestamp_ms: int,
435	        value: float,
436	        event_id: str | None = None,
437	        lookup_key: str | None = None,
438	        label_of=None,
439	    ) -> dict:
440	        """Process one event against the pre-event watermark.
441	
442	        On automatic streams every response additionally carries the
443	        post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``None`` until a watermark exists)
444	        and the ``finalized`` windows produced by this response; duplicate
445	        and dropped events leave the watermark untouched and finalize
446	        nothing. Accepted-event bookkeeping (maximum event timestamp plus
447	        the resulting monotone watermark advance) only runs after
448	        aggregation and dedup registration.
449	
450	        On joined streams the label for ``lookup_key`` is read through
451	        ``label_of`` after the dedup and lateness decisions but before
452	        any state mutation, so an unknown key (or, on a versioned table,
453	        a timestamp before the key's first version) raises with all
454	        state untouched. The dedup check includes the lookup key: an
455	        exact retry repeats timestamp, value and key, while the same id
456	        with a different key conflicts.
457	        """
458	        automatic = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms is not None
459	        joined = self.lookup_table is not None
460	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
461	            retained = self._dedup.get(event_id)
462	            if retained is not None:
463	                same = retained[0] == timestamp_ms and retained[1] == value
464	                if joined:
465	                    same = same and retained[2] == lookup_key
466	                if same:
467	                    outcome: dict = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": True}
468	                    if automatic:
469	                        outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
470	                    return outcome
471	                raise EventIdConflictError(event_id)
472	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
473	                # Unseen too-late ids are dropped without being remembered.
474	                outcome = {"dropped": True, "duplicate": False}
475	                if automatic:
476	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
477	                return outcome
478	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
479	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
480	            self._dedup[event_id] = (
481	                (timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key)
482	                if joined
483	                else (timestamp_ms, value)
484	            )
485	            outcome = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": False}
486	        else:
487	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
488	                outcome = {"dropped": True}
489	                if automatic:
490	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
491	                return outcome
492	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
493	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
494	            outcome = {"dropped": False}
495	        if automatic:
496	            newly = self._note_accepted_event(timestamp_ms)
497	            outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=newly)
498	        return outcome

500	    def apply_batch(self, events: list[dict], label_of=None) -> list[dict]:
501	        """Apply a whole batch atomically, in input order.
502	
503	        Every element goes through the regular single-event path, so
504	        dedup, lateness, lookup, window, automatic-watermark,
505	        finalization and change-feed semantics are identical to posting
506	        the events one by one; each element observes the state left by
507	        the previous ones. The first EventIdConflictError or
508	        LookupKeyNotFoundError rolls every mutation back — aggregates,
509	        dedup records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and
510	        the change sequence — so a failed batch leaves no trace.
511	        """
512	        backup = self._state_backup()
513	        outcomes: list[dict] = []
514	        try:
515	            for event in events:
516	                outcomes.append(
517	                    self.add_event(
518	                        event["timestamp_ms"],
519	                        event["value"],
520	                        event.get("event_id"),
521	                        event.get("lookup_key"),
522	                        label_of,
523	                    )
524	                )
525	        except Exception:
526	            self._state_restore(backup)
527	            raise
528	        return outcomes

559	    def _resolve_label(self, label_of, lookup_key: str | None, timestamp_ms: int):

561	
562	        The reader receives the event's own ``timestamp_ms`` so a
563	        versioned table resolves the version effective at event time; a
564	        current-value table ignores it.
565	        """

570	    def _is_too_late(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> bool:
571	        return (
572	            self.watermark is not None
573	            and timestamp_ms < self.watermark - self.allowed_lateness_ms

576	    def _note_accepted_event(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
577	        """Advance the max event timestamp and then the watermark."""
578	        if (
579	            self.max_event_timestamp is None
580	            or timestamp_ms > self.max_event_timestamp
581	        ):
582	            self.max_event_timestamp = timestamp_ms
583	        target = self.max_event_timestamp - self.auto_watermark_lag_ms
584	        if self.watermark is None or target > self.watermark:
585	            # Publish through the shared path so finalization and dedup
586	            # eviction behave exactly like a manual advance.
587	            return self.advance_watermark(target)
588	        return []

590	    def _aggregate(
591	        self,
592	        timestamp_ms: int,
593	        value: float,
594	        lookup_key: str | None = None,
595	        label: str | None = None,
596	    ) -> None:
597	        for start in self._window_starts(timestamp_ms):
598	            bucket = self._windows.setdefault(start, [0, 0])
599	            bucket[0] += 1
600	            bucket[1] += value
601	            # Base-window upsert with the post-event aggregates; sliding
602	            # streams publish one record per window, ascending by start.
603	            self._append_change("upsert", start, bucket[0], bucket[1])
604	            if self.lookup_table is not None:
605	                groups = self._joined_windows.setdefault(start, {})
606	                group = groups.setdefault((lookup_key, label), [0, 0])
607	                group[0] += 1
608	                group[1] += value

610	    def _append_change(self, kind: str, start: int, count: int, total: float) -> None:
611	        """Publish one change-feed record and trim to the retention cap.
612	
613	        Sequence numbers are handed out consecutively from 1 and never
614	        regress; trimming only drops the oldest retained records.
615	        """
616	        if self.change_retention is None:
617	            return
618	        self._latest_seq += 1
619	        self._changes.append(
620	            {
621	                "seq": self._latest_seq,
622	                "kind": kind,
623	                "window_start_ms": start,
624	                "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
625	                "count": count,
626	                "sum": total,
627	            }
628	        )
629	        overflow = len(self._changes) - self.change_retention
630	        if overflow > 0:
631	            del self._changes[:overflow]

633	    def advance_watermark(self, watermark_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
634	        if self.watermark is not None and watermark_ms < self.watermark:
635	            raise WatermarkRegressionError(
636	                f"watermark {watermark_ms} is below current {self.watermark}"
637	            )
638	        self.watermark = watermark_ms
639	        newly: list[dict] = []
640	        for start in sorted(self._windows):
641	            if start in self._finalized_starts:
642	                continue
643	            end = start + self.window_ms
644	            if watermark_ms >= end + self.allowed_lateness_ms:
645	                count, total = self._windows[start]
646	                newly.append(
647	                    {
648	                        "stream": self.name,
649	                        "window_start_ms": start,
650	                        "window_end_ms": end,
651	                        "count": count,
652	                        "sum": total,
653	                    }
654	                )
655	                self._finalized_starts.add(start)
656	                # The final record of a window always follows every
657	                # upsert of the triggering commit.
658	                self._append_change("final", start, count, total)
659	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
660	                    # Joined groups finalize synchronously with their window,
661	                    # ordered by (lookup_key, label) within it.
662	                    groups = self._joined_windows.pop(start, {})
663	                    for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
664	                        group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
665	                        self._joined_finalized.append(
666	                            {
667	                                "stream": self.name,
668	                                "window_start_ms": start,
669	                                "window_end_ms": end,
670	                                "lookup_key": key,
671	                                "label": group_label,
672	                                "count": group_count,
673	                                "sum": group_sum,
674	                            }
675	                        )
676	        self._finalized.extend(newly)
677	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
678	            horizon = watermark_ms - self.dedup_retention_ms
679	            self._dedup = {
680	                event_id: kept
681	                for event_id, kept in self._dedup.items()
682	                if kept[0] >= horizon
683	            }
684	        return newly
685	
686	    def results(self) -> list[dict]:
687	        return [dict(row) for row in self._finalized]

689	    def to_snapshot(self) -> dict:
690	        """Serialize this stream as one entry of a version-1 snapshot."""
691	        entry: dict = {
692	            "name": self.name,
693	            "window_ms": self.window_ms,
694	            "allowed_lateness_ms": self.allowed_lateness_ms,
695	            "dedup_retention_ms": self.dedup_retention_ms,
696	            "watermark_ms": self.watermark,
697	            "windows": [
698	                {
699	                    "window_start_ms": start,
700	                    "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
701	                    "count": self._windows[start][0],
702	                    "sum": self._windows[start][1],
703	                }
704	                for start in sorted(self._windows)
705	                if start not in self._finalized_starts
706	            ],
707	            "finalized": sorted(
708	                (dict(row) for row in self._finalized),
709	                key=lambda row: row["window_start_ms"],
710	            ),
711	        }
712	        if self.auto_watermark_lag_ms is not None:
713	            # Automatic streams publish the pair together; manual streams
714	            # keep the historical document shape exactly.
715	            entry["auto_watermark_lag_ms"] = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms
716	            entry["max_event_timestamp_ms"] = self.max_event_timestamp
717	        if self.slide_ms is not None:
718	            # Sliding streams publish the step; documents without it
719	            # restore as tumbling streams.
720	            entry["slide_ms"] = self.slide_ms
721	        if self.lookup_table is not None:
722	            # Joined streams publish the table reference plus the grouped
723	            # state; only format_version 2 documents may carry these.
724	            entry["lookup_table"] = self.lookup_table
725	            joined_open = []
726	            for start in sorted(self._joined_windows):
727	                groups = self._joined_windows[start]
728	                for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
729	                    group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
730	                    joined_open.append(
731	                        {
732	                            "window_start_ms": start,
733	                            "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
734	                            "lookup_key": key,
735	                            "label": group_label,
736	                            "count": group_count,
737	                            "sum": group_sum,
738	                        }
739	                    )
740	            entry["joined_windows"] = joined_open
741	            entry["joined_finalized"] = [dict(row) for row in self._joined_finalized]
742	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
743	            records = []
744	            for event_id, kept in sorted(self._dedup.items()):
745	                record = {
746	                    "event_id": event_id,
747	                    "timestamp_ms": kept[0],
748	                    "value": kept[1],
749	                }
750	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
751	                    record["lookup_key"] = kept[2]
752	                records.append(record)
753	            entry["dedup_records"] = records
754	        if self.change_retention is not None:
755	            # Change-feed streams publish the config, the cursor and the
756	            # retained records; only format_version 3 documents may carry
757	            # these.
758	            entry["change_retention"] = self.change_retention
759	            entry["latest_seq"] = self._latest_seq
760	            entry["changes"] = [dict(record) for record in self._changes]
761	        if self.batch_retention is not None:
762	            # Batch-enabled streams publish the config plus the retained
763	            # batch records in commit order; only format_version 4
764	            # documents may carry these.
765	            entry["batch_retention"] = self.batch_retention
766	            entry["batches"] = copy.deepcopy(self._batches)
767	        return entry

1064	    @staticmethod
1065	    def _parse_window_list(
1066	        value: object,
1067	        name: str,
1068	        window_ms: int,
1069	        where: str,
1070	        *,
1071	        with_stream: bool,
1072	        step_ms: int | None = None,
1073	    ) -> list[dict]:
1074	        if not isinstance(value, list):
1075	            raise SnapshotError(f"stream {name!r}: {where} must be an array")
1076	        if step_ms is None:
1077	            step_ms = window_ms
1078	        fields = (
1079	            {"stream", "window_start_ms", "window_end_ms", "count", "sum"}
1080	            if with_stream
1081	            else {"window_start_ms", "window_end_ms", "count", "sum"}
1082	        )
1083	        rows: list[dict] = []
1084	        previous: int | None = None
1085	        for raw in value:
1086	            if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1087	                raise SnapshotError(f"stream {name!r}: {where} entries must be objects")
1088	            extra = sorted(set(raw) - fields)
1089	            if extra:
1090	                raise SnapshotError(
1091	                    f"stream {name!r}: {where} entry has unexpected field: {extra[0]}"
1092	                )
1093	            missing = sorted(fields - set(raw))
1094	            if missing:
1095	                raise SnapshotError(
1096	                    f"stream {name!r}: {where} entry missing field: {missing[0]}"
1097	                )
1098	            start = raw["window_start_ms"]

"""Core service surface for StreamMill.

The frozen baseline only reports process health; that surface stays
unchanged. On top of it this module now implements named event-time
tumbling windows with explicit watermarks:

* streams are created with a positive ``window_ms`` and a non-negative
  ``allowed_lateness_ms``;
* events carry an integer ``timestamp_ms`` and a finite numeric ``value``
  and land in the left-closed, right-open window
  ``[floor(timestamp_ms / window_ms) * window_ms, +window_ms)``;
* a per-stream watermark only moves forward; once it reaches
  ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` the window is final, is
  emitted exactly once, and is retained for queries;
* events with ``timestamp_ms < watermark - allowed_lateness_ms`` are
  acknowledged but dropped without touching the aggregates.

Streams may optionally be created with a positive ``slide_ms`` (no
larger than ``window_ms`` and dividing it evenly). Such streams use
fixed-step overlapping sliding windows: an accepted event at timestamp
``t`` is counted once in every window ``[start, start + window_ms)``
whose ``start`` is an integer multiple of ``slide_ms`` and satisfies
``start <= t < start + window_ms`` (negative timestamps follow the same
mathematical grid). Every window still finalizes independently once the
watermark reaches its own ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` and is
emitted exactly once, ordered by window start. Without ``slide_ms`` the
stream is the plain tumbling stream above and every public shape is
unchanged.

Streams may optionally enable event-id deduplication by passing a
positive ``dedup_retention_ms`` (no smaller than ``allowed_lateness_ms``)
at creation time. On such streams every event must carry a non-empty
string ``event_id``:

* the first occurrence of an id is aggregated and remembered together
  with its ``timestamp_ms`` and ``value``;
* an exact retry (same ``timestamp_ms`` and numerically equal ``value``)
  is reported as ``duplicate: true`` and never touches the aggregates —
  the dedup check runs before the lateness check, so retained retries
  are duplicates even past the lateness horizon;
* the same id with a different timestamp or value is rejected with
  ``event_id_conflict`` and leaves all state untouched;
* an unseen id that arrives too late is dropped as usual and its id is
  not remembered.

Remembered ids are evicted once the watermark advances past
``timestamp_ms + dedup_retention_ms`` (ids exactly on the boundary are
kept); evicted ids may be reused and are treated as new events.

Streams created with a non-negative ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` track the
maximum ``timestamp_ms`` of every successfully accepted event. After an
event is aggregated (and its id registered, when deduplicating) the
watermark advances atomically to
``max(current_watermark, max_event_timestamp - auto_watermark_lag_ms)``;
the lateness/dedup decision for that event uses the watermark as it was
before the advance. Dropped, duplicate or conflicting events never move
the maximum event timestamp or the watermark. Manual watermark posts keep
working on automatic streams and subsequent automatic advances never
regress below a manual watermark. Event responses on automatic streams
additionally carry the post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``null`` until a
watermark exists) and the windows finalized by that response.

A portable full-state snapshot is available through
``Service.snapshot`` / ``Service.restore_snapshot``: export produces a
self-contained JSON document (``format_version`` 1) capturing config,
watermark, open windows, finalized results and retained dedup records;
automatic streams additionally carry ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` and
``max_event_timestamp_ms``; sliding streams additionally carry
``slide_ms`` (a document without it restores as a tumbling stream).
Restore is only accepted on an instance
without any streams, validates the document strictly (never silently
repairing it) and publishes the whole state atomically.

In-process dimension tables provide the lookup side of an optional
current-value stream-table join:

* ``POST /tables`` creates a named table; rows are written with
  ``PUT``-style upserts of non-empty string ``key``/``label`` pairs and
  report whether the stored label actually ``changed``;
* a stream may be created with ``lookup_table`` naming an existing
  table. Events on such a stream must carry a non-empty ``lookup_key``;
  after the usual dedup and lateness decisions the current label is read
  atomically (an unknown key is rejected with ``lookup_key_not_found``
  and leaves all state untouched) and the event is aggregated both into
  the plain windows and into per-window ``(lookup_key, label)`` groups.
  Later table writes only affect later events. Dedup records on joined
  streams include the ``lookup_key``, so resubmitting an id with a
  different key is an ``event_id_conflict``;
* joined groups finalize together with their window and are exposed
  through ``Service.joined_results``, ordered by window start, lookup
  key and label.

Snapshots export as ``format_version`` 2 (adding ``tables`` plus
``lookup_table``/``joined_windows``/``joined_finalized`` on joined
streams) whenever any table exists, and restore stays compatible with
version 1 documents. When the join is unused every public shape and the
version 1 snapshot are unchanged.

Streams may optionally materialize a window change feed by passing a
positive ``change_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the create
response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before). On such
streams every state change is published as a totally ordered sequence of
records, numbered by a ``seq`` that starts at 1 and never regresses:

* every successfully aggregated event appends one ``upsert`` record per
  affected base window (ascending by window start on sliding streams),
  carrying the post-event ``count``/``sum`` of that window;
* every watermark advance that finalizes windows appends one ``final``
  record per newly finalized window (ascending by window start) with the
  final aggregates — on automatic streams the upserts of the triggering
  event always precede the finals of the resulting advance, and an
  advance without newly finalized windows appends nothing;
* duplicates, too-late drops, conflicts, unknown lookup keys and
  validation failures never consume a sequence number, and joined
  streams publish only the base-window changes.

``Service.changes`` returns the retained records with ``seq`` greater
than a cursor, ascending, together with the current ``latest_seq``.
Only the newest ``change_retention`` records are kept (older ones are
trimmed after every commit, without moving ``latest_seq``); a cursor
past ``latest_seq`` raises ChangeCursorAheadError and a cursor that has
fallen behind the oldest retained record raises
ChangeCursorExpiredError.

Instances with at least one change-feed stream export snapshots as
``format_version`` 3, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
enabled streams, ``change_retention``/``latest_seq``/``changes``.
Restore validates the retained records strictly (sequence continuity
against ``latest_seq`` and the retention cap, ordering, window
alignment, and the last retained record of every window against the
aggregated state) and publishes the feed so the cursor and the next
sequence number continue exactly as on the uninterrupted instance.
Version 1 and 2 documents restore as before, and instances without a
change feed keep exporting their original versions and shapes.

Streams may optionally enable recoverable atomic batch ingestion by
passing a positive ``batch_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the
create response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before and the
batch entry point raises BatchIngestNotEnabledError). On such streams
``Service.add_batch`` accepts a non-empty ``batch_id`` plus 1 to 1000
events that each follow the stream's single-event rules:

* the whole batch is applied at one consistent point, in input order and
  under the service lock, reusing the per-event dedup, lateness, lookup,
  window, automatic-watermark, finalization and change-feed semantics —
  no concurrent request can observe an intermediate state, and on
  automatic streams each element sees the watermark left by the
  previous one;
* the first event-id conflict or unknown lookup key aborts the batch and
  rolls back every state the earlier elements touched (aggregates, dedup
  records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and change
  sequence), so a failed batch leaves the stream exactly as before and
  does not occupy its identifier; too-late drops and exact duplicates
  remain successful outcomes;
* a successful batch is remembered together with its request and full
  response. Within the retention a retry carrying the same field values
  in the same event order replays the stored response without writing
  again (and without refreshing the retention order), while the same
  ``batch_id`` with different content raises BatchIdConflictError. Only
  the newest ``batch_retention`` records are kept; evicted identifiers
  may be reused, and concurrent submissions of one identifier commit at
  most once.

Instances with at least one batch-enabled stream export snapshots as
``format_version`` 4, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
enabled streams, ``batch_retention`` plus the retained batch records in
commit order. Restore validates the records strictly (identifier
uniqueness, the retention cap, and the request/response shapes against
the stream's features) and publishes them so replay and eviction behave
exactly as on the uninterrupted instance. Older document versions
restore as before.

Dimension tables may optionally be declared event-time versioned by
passing ``event_time_versioned: true`` at creation time (echoed in the
create response; without it the table keeps the current-value overwrite
semantics above and every public shape is unchanged). A versioned table
receives rows of ``key``/``label``/``effective_from_ms`` through the
same row entry point: each version of a key is effective from its
``effective_from_ms`` until the key's next version, writes may arrive
out of order, a first write or a new effective time reports
``changed: true``, an identical retry reports ``changed: false``, and
an existing ``(key, effective_from_ms)`` point resubmitted with a
different label raises DimensionVersionConflictError and leaves the
history untouched. A stream whose ``lookup_table`` is versioned
resolves every event's label as the newest version with
``effective_from_ms <= timestamp_ms`` — late-arriving or backfilled
history therefore only affects events whose own event time it precedes
and never recomputes already received events; an unknown key or an
event time before the key's first version raises
LookupVersionNotFoundError with all state untouched. Dedup, lateness,
windowing, watermarks, change-feed sequence numbers and batch
atomicity (a missing version anywhere rolls the whole batch back) are
exactly as on current-value joins.

Instances with at least one versioned table export snapshots as
``format_version`` 5, which always carries the ``tables`` array; each
table object records its mode, and versioned tables export their rows
as ``versions`` strictly ordered by ``key`` then ``effective_from_ms``.
Restore stays compatible with versions 1 to 4 and validates version 5
strictly (mode field combinations, duplicate or out-of-order versions,
invalid effective times and conflicting points all raise SnapshotError
without publishing partial state).

Disk persistence remains out of scope.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import copy
import math
import threading

from . import __version__

SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION = 1
SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION_JOIN = 2
SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION_CHANGES = 3
SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION_BATCHES = 4
SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION_VERSIONED_TABLES = 5


class StreamExistsError(Exception):
    """Raised when creating a stream that already exists."""


class StreamNotFoundError(Exception):
    """Raised when addressing a stream that does not exist."""


class TableExistsError(Exception):
    """Raised when creating a table that already exists."""


class TableNotFoundError(Exception):
    """Raised when addressing a table that does not exist."""


class LookupKeyNotFoundError(Exception):
    """Raised when an event's lookup_key has no row in the table."""


class DimensionVersionConflictError(Exception):
    """Raised when an existing version point is rewritten with a new label."""


class LookupVersionNotFoundError(Exception):

class JoinNotEnabledError(Exception):
    """Raised when querying joined results on a plain stream."""


class ChangeFeedNotEnabledError(Exception):
    """Raised when reading the change feed of a stream without one."""


class ChangeCursorAheadError(Exception):
    """Raised when a change cursor is past the latest sequence number."""


class ChangeCursorExpiredError(Exception):
    """Raised when a change cursor fell behind the retained records."""
